message.content: I'll buy Electric Company. One hundred fifty still leaves me liquid, and it keeps the utility pair out of p3's hands.
message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to buy Electric Company or start an auction.

I have $1012 and own four properties. p3 already owns Water Works, so owning both utilities would triple the rent. I should buy Electric Company.

A single utility is poor value. Average rent is only about $28, so the $150 cost is expensive for the return. I previously skipped incomplete groups to stay liquid. I should probably pass on this.

I cannot complete the utility set without Water Works. p3 likely wants this property to finish their monopoly, so an auction would probably end with them owning it. I should keep cash for stronger color groups instead.

A utility monopoly averages about $70 in rent, which is decent but weaker than color monopolies with houses. Denying p3 this set is strategically valuable because they lead in cash at $1435. Still, completing my own color monopolies remains the higher priority.

I own one light blue and one orange property. I still need Oriental and Connecticut for the light blue set, and New York or Tennessee for the orange set.

St. Charles belongs to the pink group, not orange. New York and Tennessee remain available for my orange set.

I could trade Electric Company to p3 later for a property I need. They do not own anything that completes my color sets, so the utility would have little trade value.

I can still afford New York, Illinois, and Tennessee after spending $150 on Electric Company. This is different from the yellow properties I previously skipped, since I own no yellows and no opponent immediately monopolizes that group.

I will buy Electric Company. An auction would likely end with p3 winning the property anyway, so I should take the cheap denial now rather than risk overpaying or losing it.
